THESE APPEALS ARE COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  JUDGMENT

The appeal and the cross-objection have been preferred challenging the judgment and award passed by Prl.Civil Judge and Addl M.A.C.T., Saundatti, at Saundatti (hereinafter referred as 'tribunal' for short) in MVC No.1057/2010 dated 06.06.2012.
2.

entities.text: Prl.Civil Judge and Addl M.A.C.T., Saundatti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appeal preferred by the Insurance Company is premised on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded by the tribunal and seeking for reduction of the same.
Whereas, the cross-objection preferred by the claimants is premised on the ground of inadequacy and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Consequently, seeking for enhancement of compensation.

3. Brief Facts of the case, 3.1 The unfortunate incident of road traffic accident in the present case has rendered the claimant Siddayya S/o Gangappa @ Maharudrayya Betsurmath incapable and immobile for the rest of his life forcing him to be bedridden for the remaining part of his life.

On 21.08.2009, when the claimant who was working as a conductor in the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-22/B-9399 while on his duty from Hubli-Ilakal in the route assigned left the Ilakal at about 8:00 p.m and reached Badami at about 11:20 p.m.

Some of the passengers alighted at Badami and when the bus reached the railway station road at about 11:30 p.m., on Badami-Guledagudda road, the driver of the vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and safety and dashed to a road side Neelagiri tree and caused the accident.

Due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus in which the claimant was the conductor,
sustained severe grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately thereafter, the claimant was admitted to Community Health Centre, Badami where he took first aid treatment.
Later, he was shifted to Kerudi Hospital, Bagalakote, wherein he was inpatient from 22.08.2009 to 24.08.2009.
Subsequently, the claimant was admitted to Vivekanand General Hospital, Deshpande Nagar, Hubli wherein he was inpatient from 24.08.2009 to 12.09.2009 and underwent operation.

entities.text: Vivekanand General Hospital, Deshpande Nagar, Hubli
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Again the claimant was admitted to Navadagi Hospital, Saundatti on 12.9.2009 and thereafter, he was admitted to Kulgod Multi Specialty Hospital, Ramdurg from 11.10.2009 to 12.11.2010.
3.2 It is stated that the claimant underwent several surgeries and operations and expended huge financial amount towards the medical treatment and follow up treatment.
It is further stated that prior to the occurrence of accident, claimant was working as a conductor in the offending bus and was earning Rs.8,000/- per month and maintaining his family.
He was unmarried and aged about 22 years.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, claimant is permanently disabled and he is bedridden for life.
The movements of both the legs are restricted, he cannot stand, walk or sit and The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ...

3 requires two attendants on a daily basis for his day to day activities.

As earlier stated, claimant is a bachelor thereby he has lost the marriage prospects and due to the enormous injuries suffered in the accident, he is mentally depressed and has suffered enormously both physically and financially.

In view of having sustained serious permanent disability forcing the claimant to be bedridden for the remaining part of his life and having incurred huge financial expenditures, the claimant filed claim petition, seeking compensation.

3.3 On notice being served to respondents, who appeared before the Court and filed their statement of objections inter-alia denying the occurrence of accident, rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending bus.

The respondents also denied the age, avocation and income of the claimant,
apart from denying exorbitant amount of compensation sought for by the claimant.

It is also pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving license,
as on the date of occurrence of accident and further the driver of the bus had violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
On the basis of these pleadings, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal has framed relevant issues for consideration.

5. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined three other witnesses including one Doctor-Dr.Sanjeev Kalasur as PW.4 and got marked documents as Exs.P.1 to P.538.
Whereas, the respondents have not adduced any evidence.
However, they got marked the insurance policy as Ex.R.1 with the consent of parties.

6. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the arguments of learned counsel appearing for both the parties, the tribunal awarded the total compensation of Rs.21,21,000/- to the claimant with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition.
7. Being aggrieved by the exorbitant, unreasonable compensation awarded, the insurance company has preferred appeal challenging the judgment and award of the tribunal.
Being aggrieved by the inadequacy and meager compensation awarded, the claimant has preferred cross-objection seeking enhancement of compensation.

It is vehement contention of learned counsel Shri G.N.Raichur,
appearing on behalf of the appellant-Insurer that the tribunal has committed a serious error in awarding huge and exorbitant compensation contrary to the material evidence placed on record both oral and documentary.
He further contends that the tribunal has grossly erred in considering the disability to an extent of 100% believing the evidence of PW.4-Dr. Sanjeev Kalasur.

Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has gone on a tangent by awarding excess compensation under various heads without keeping in mind the award of compensation towards disability at 100%.
He contends that the tribunal has erred in awarding compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

When already the tribunal has arrived at compensation towards loss of income due to disability at 100%, the question of awarding further compensation under the head of loss of amenities would not arise and that runs contrary to the principles of awarding loss of income due to the disability.

Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has also erred in awarding other compensation under the head pain and suffering, attendant charges, conveyance, incidental charges,
future medical expenses, which are highly exorbitant and the same requires to be set-aside, as it is against the intent of legislation in awarding the compensation under the guise of just and reasonable compensation.
9.

Learned counsel further contends that the tribunal has committed a gross error in awarding future medical expenses and thereby the total compensation being highly exorbitant and unreasonable, the same requires to be set aside.

Learned counsel further contends that while awarding compensation tribunal and this Court will have to consider reasonable and just compensation to be awarded rather than the compensation being a luxury to the claimant and becoming a huge loss to the insurance company.

On these grounds learned counsel for the appellant seeks to allow this appeal, consequently set aside the judgment and award of the tribunal and reduce the compensation by awarding just and reasonable compensation.

10. Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimant who has preferred cross objection has sought for enhancement of compensation in view of - 10 - the compensation being meager and inadequate.
It is his vehement contention that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is arbitrary, unreasonable and wholly erroneous and contrary to the material evidence placed on record.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the claimant that he suffered permanent physical disability and has thereby lost the capacity to work or earn in future and that due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending bus, the young and energetic adolescent man, claimant herein has been rendered immobile and incapable for the rest of his life to be forced to be bedridden and to be dependent on other persons for remaining part of his life.

11. It is vehement contention of the learned counsel that though tribunal has accepted the disability to an extent of 100%, the tribunal has committed a gross error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation under several heads.

It is his primary contention that the tribunal has failed to take into account the proper income for assessment of loss of future income and has committed an error in taking the income at only - 11 - Rs.4,500/- per month, whereas, the claimant has adduced evidence by stating that he was a conductor by profession while he was on his duty as a conductor, traveling from Hubballi to Ilkal and back, he suffered the injuries rendering him bedridden for the remaining part of his life due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

It is the contention of the claimant that though he was earning Rs.8,000/- per month, the tribunal has failed to take into consideration the said amount for assessment of compensation, thereby the tribunal has committed a serious error in calculation of compensation towards loss of income towards permanent disability.

sentences.text: It is further contended by the learned counsel for the claimant that due to the claimant being rendered bedridden and disabled for the remaining part of his life, the future marriage prospects of the claimant has been totally diminished and there is absolutely no scope for any marriage prospect for the claimant, which aspect has been ignored and not considered and no amount of compensation is awarded under this head.

Learned - 12 - counsel also contends that the tribunal has failed to take into consideration awarding of future prospects while granting compensation, which is another serious error committed by the tribunal.

He also contends that the claimant admittedly was inpatient in the hospital for more than a year and the tribunal has not awarded reasonable compensation towards loss of income during the laid up period.

He further contends that the tribunal has lost sight of the fact the claimant is now rendered helpless and dependent on another person to do is day to day activities which aspect has also been ignored and no amount of compensation is awarded by the tribunal for attendant to attend to the future life of the claimant, which requires 24 x 7 treatment by the attendant.
On these aspects the learned counsel seeks to allow his cross objection and consequently enhance the compensation substantially as claimed in the claim petition.

13. Having heard the learned counsel for the insurer Shri G.N.Raichur and the learned counsel for the - 13 - claimant Shri H.M.Dharigond, the points that arise for consideration before this Court are as under:
i) Whether the tribunal has committed error in awarding exorbitant compensation to the claimant?
 ii) Whether the tribunal has awarded  inadequate and meager compensation  to the claimant?
 iii) Whether the tribunal has not  considered the relevant aspects for determination of compensation to be in the form of just and reasonable compensation?
iv) What order?
14.

It is not in dispute that on 21.8.2009 when the claimant was travelling in the bus,
as mentioned above as a conductor doing his official duty, the driver of the said bus drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and dashed against a Nilgiri Tree and caused the accident.

It The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/
6 is not in dispute that due to the accident the claimant suffered injuries.

sentences.text:
. In order to substantiate that the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of the bus, and that he was responsible for rash and negligent driving, the claimant has produced Exs.P.1 to P.5,
which are all police records.
The evidentiary value of Exs.P.1 to P.5 cannot be ignored and the same is accepted as there is no evidence to the contrary to disprove the veracity and genuineness of Exs.P.1 to P.5.

Therefore, this Court would not want to delve into the details of occurrence of accident, rash and negligence and cause of accident and the criminal case having been registered against the driver of the offending bus, which are exhibited in P.1 to P.5 and the same is not disputed.
16. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the claimant, it is not disputed that the claimant as on the date of occurrence of accident was aged 22 years.
It is also an admitted fact that the claimant was working as conductor in the same bus which met with accident.
However it is seriously disputed by the learned counsel for insurer with regard to the income of the claimant.

As claimant was aged 22 years on the date of accident appropriate multiplier would be 18 which is rightly applied by the tribunal, which is not seriously disputed by the learned counsel for insurance company.
18. The tribunal has taken income of the claimant at Rs.150/- per day and consequently assessed the income at Rs.4,500/- per month.

I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the claimant that the accident having occurred in the year 2005, the notional income chart prescribes a standard income of Rs.5,000/- as stipulated by the Legal Services Authority for determination of income,
where there is no proof of income produced by the parties.

Therefore, the income necessarily requires to be taken at Rs.5,000/- in the present case in consonance to the chart, as against Rs.4,500/- per month adopted by the tribunal as the tribunal and this Court will have to do guess work when there is no proof of income and in order to do a standard guess work, the Legal Services Authority formulated a prescribed notional income chart which requires to be adopted in such cases.
Accordingly Rs.5,000/- is taken as - 16 - income of the claimant.
The multiplier has been rightly adopted by the tribunal at 18 for the age group of claimant being 22 years which is not disputed and the same is kept intact.

The claimant has got examined the doctor as PW.4 who has assessed and opined that the claimant has suffered a total disability of 100% as there is absolutely no sensation in the lower limb of the body and the same has been opined by the doctor PW.4 who is a neuro surgeon who treated the claimant.

Therefore,
disability is assessed at 100% towards the whole body as the claimant is rendered bedridden for the remaining part of his life.

In view of this Court assessing income of the claimant at Rs.5,000/- per month, the future prospects at 40% will have to be added in consonance to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680.
20.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

In view of the above, the total loss of income due to permanent disability is calculated as under:
- 17 - Rs.5,000/- + 40% x 12 x 18 x 100% = Rs.15,12,000/-, as against Rs.9,72,000/-
awarded by the tribunal.

21. It is seen that though the tribunal has accepted the expert opinion of the doctor PW.4 with regard to permanent disability suffered by the claimant, tribunal has not awarded any amount for the assistance of attendant which would be mandatory for the claimant for the remaining part of his life.

The learned counsel for the claimant says, at least Rs.4,000/- would be required for engaging at least one attendant to take care of the claimant at 24 x 7 basis for day to day activities of the claimant.
I am of the opinion that it would be on higher side.
Hence this Court is of the opinion that at least Rs.3,000/- per month would be required to be awarded which would be inconsonance with the minimum wages adopted by the State.

Therefore, if Rs.3,000/- is taken as the salary to be paid,
the same on calculation would be Rs.6,48,000/- (Rs.3,000/- x 12 x 18) would be the amount that would have to be paid to the attendant who - 18 - is required 24 x 7 basis to take care the needs of the claimant for the remaining part of his life.
22. The tribunal has awarded medical expenses of Rs.3,49,000/- on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant at Exs.P.112 to P.213 and Exs.P.321 to P.526, which are the actual bills.
The tribunal has rightly awarded the amount and the same does not call for interference.
Hence the same is left intact.
23. Towards attendant charges in the hospital, food, conveyance and other incidental charges, the tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- each and in all Rs.2,00,000/-.

Considering the fact that the claimant was admitted as an inpatient in the hospital for more than a year, I am of the opinion that the amount of compensation awarded under these heads is just and reasonable and the same does not call for further indulgence.
Hence the same is left intact.
24. The tribunal has not awarded any amount of compensation to the claimant under the head loss of marriage prospects.

The tribunal has lost sight of the fact that the man aged 22 years has been left bedridden for - 19 - The Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance ... vs Siddayya S/O Gangappa @ Maharudrayya ... on 7 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130776039/
8 the remaining part of his life who would not be able to enjoy the life of Grihasthashrama (married person).

sentences.text:
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to award compensation to the extent of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards loss of marriage prospects.
25. Towards pain and suffering, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- which I am of the opinion is on lower side.
The same requires to be enhanced.

The learned counsel for the insurer vehemently contends relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, for the purpose of not awarding any amount of compensation under the head pain and suffering and loss of amenities on the ground that when 100% disability is taken, question of awarding further compensation under these two heads does not arise.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, I am afraid that the contention put forth by the learned counsel for the insurer cannot be accepted for the reason that no amount of monetary compensation can heal the mental scar of pain and agony suffered and undertaken or met by the claimant presently or in future - 20 - on the basis of day to day activities.
These monetary amounts could be only a solace to the claimant to meet his expenses and it cannot bring back the original life of claimant with similar enthusiasm and energy in life.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the claimant would be entitled to an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering as against Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
26. Towards loss of amenities, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- and towards future medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/-.

The learned counsel for the insurer vehemently contends that the said amount awarded by the tribunal itself is exorbitant and the same does not require further enhancement and he continues to rely on the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar vs.
Ajay Kumar (supra).
27.

Having gone through the detailed analysis made by the Hon'ble Apex Court, what needs to be considered is whether the appellant will be able to live his life with the amount of pain and agony and the amenities that he has lost due to the incapacity and permanently - 21 - being bedridden due to the accident caused in the road traffic.
As stated earlier no amount of compensation can fulfill the requirement of the claimant.

However, it cannot be disputed by the insurer, the claimant being aged 22 years as on the date of occurrence of accident, he would have gone on to live for another 30 years and if he was leading a normal life, he would have enjoyed the life fully.

In view of he being rendered incapacitated bedridden for the remaining part of his life, it cannot be denied that the claimant is deprived to live a normal life as a normal human being to enjoy his life.
Therefore, it would be reasonable to award a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- under the head loss of amenities for enjoyment of life and under the head future medical expenses.

Therefore, an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- is awarded as against Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by the tribunal under the head loss of amenities and Rs.2,00,000/- awarded under the head towards future medical expenses.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for a total compensation of Rs.42,09,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer submits that the Court cannot grant compensation more than what is claimed by the claimant.
However, it is hard to countenance such an argument by the insurance company for the reason that the enactment of M.V.Act is a welfare legislation to do the benefit to the injured/victim/dependants.
The claimant has suffered 100% disability, no amount of compensation can bring back the normal life of the young man.
He is now disabled and bedridden for the remaining - 23 - part of his life.
Hence the same is negatived.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal in MFA No.24921/2012 preferred by the insurance company is dismissed.
 ii) The cross objection in MFA CROB  No.100109/2015 preferred by the  claimant is allowed.

 iv) The claimant is entitled to a total  compensation of Rs.42,09,000/- as against Rs.21,21,000/- awarded by the tribunal.

v) The respondent insurer shall pay the enhanced compensation with interest - 24 - at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, to be deposited before the jurisdictional tribunal.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The appeal preferred by the Insurance Company is premised on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded by the tribunal and seeking for reduction of the same.
Consequently, seeking for enhancement of compensation.
Some of the passengers alighted at Badami and when the bus reached the railway station road at about 11:30 p.m., on Badami-Guledagudda road, the driver of the vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and safety and dashed to a road side Neelagiri tree and caused the accident.
Due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus in which the claimant was the conductor,
sustained severe grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately thereafter, the claimant was admitted to Community Health Centre, Badami where he took first aid treatment.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
He contends that the tribunal has erred in awarding compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.
The learned counsel for the insurer vehemently contends relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another, reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, for the purpose of not awarding any amount of compensation under the head pain and suffering and loss of amenities on the ground that when 100% disability is taken, question of awarding further compensation under these two heads does not arise.
These monetary amounts could be only a solace to the claimant to meet his expenses and it cannot bring back the original life of claimant with similar enthusiasm and energy in life.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the claimant that the accident having occurred in the year 2005, the notional income chart prescribes a standard income of Rs.5,000/- as stipulated by the Legal Services Authority for determination of income,
where there is no proof of income produced by the parties.
Therefore, the income necessarily requires to be taken at Rs.5,000/- in the present case in consonance to the chart, as against Rs.4,500/- per month adopted by the tribunal as the tribunal and this Court will have to do guess work when there is no proof of income and in order to do a standard guess work, the Legal Services Authority formulated a prescribed notional income chart which requires to be adopted in such cases.
Accordingly Rs.5,000/- is taken as - 16 - income of the claimant.
The multiplier has been rightly adopted by the tribunal at 18 for the age group of claimant being 22 years which is not disputed and the same is kept intact.
Therefore,
disability is assessed at 100% towards the whole body as the claimant is rendered bedridden for the remaining part of his life.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the claimant would be entitled to an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering as against Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
As stated earlier no amount of compensation can fulfill the requirement of the claimant.
However, it cannot be disputed by the insurer, the claimant being aged 22 years as on the date of occurrence of accident, he would have gone on to live for another 30 years and if he was leading a normal life, he would have enjoyed the life fully.
In view of he being rendered incapacitated bedridden for the remaining part of his life, it cannot be denied that the claimant is deprived to live a normal life as a normal human being to enjoy his life.
The claimant has suffered 100% disability, no amount of compensation can bring back the normal life of the young man.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to award compensation to the extent of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards loss of marriage prospects.
25. Towards pain and suffering, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- which I am of the opinion is on lower side.
26. Towards loss of amenities, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- and towards future medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/-.
Therefore, it would be reasonable to award a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- under the head loss of amenities for enjoyment of life and under the head future medical expenses.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- is awarded as against Rs.2,00,000/- awarded by the tribunal under the head loss of amenities and Rs.2,00,000/- awarded under the head towards future medical expenses.
In view of the same, the claimant is entitled to enhancement of compensation as per the table mentioned hereunder.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal in MFA No.24921/2012 preferred by the insurance company is dismissed.

viii) No order as to costs.
